options: The community of trillions of microbes living in and on your body
questions.explanation: The microbiome is the whole community of trillions of microbes - mostly bacteria - that live in and on your body.
questions.misconception: Some think the microbiome is a single germ or a vitamin, but it is a whole population of microbes living on and in you.

questions.prompt: What do most of the microbiome members live?
options: In the gut (intestines), and on the skin
questions.explanation: The biggest microbial community lives in the gut, with more on the skin and mouth - a world of microbes on and in you.
questions.misconception: People often think the microbiome lives only in one odd place; actually most resides in the gut and on the skin.

questions.prompt: Which is a helpful job your microbiome does?
options: Helps digest food and makes some vitamins
questions.explanation: Your helpful gut microbes aid digestion, make some vitamins, train the immune system, and crowd out harmful germs.
questions.misconception: The idea that microbes such as the microbiome are all harmful is wrong - these are mostly helpful partners in body function.

questions.prompt: How can the microbiome be harmed?
options: By antibiotics killing many of the microbes and an unbalanced diet
By eating more fiber and vegetables
questions.explanation: Strong antibiotics can kill many good microbes and an unbalanced diet can stress them, breaking the balance, while eating fiber helps the gut.
questions.misconception: A healthy microbiome actually benefits from fiber, vegetables, and careful antibiotic use; endless antibiotic overuse is what can harm its balance.
